hotel.name: The Beachcomber Hotel & Resort
hotel.hero_subtitle: An iconic Hamptons-inspired waterfront retreat on the shores of Tuggerah Lake, anchoring the laid-back coastal heart of Toukley on the NSW Central Coast.
hotel.description_p1: The Beachcomber Hotel & Resort, affectionately known to locals as 'The Beachie', is a long-standing Central Coast landmark reimagined as a boutique waterfront destination. Sitting directly on the edge of Tuggerah Lake in the seaside town of Toukley, it pairs sweeping water views with a breezy Hamptons-inspired aesthetic of timber, rattan and soft coastal tones. The Beachcomber forms part of the Ascend Hotel Collection and is one of the most loved meeting places on this stretch of coast.
hotel.description_p2: Accommodation ranges from comfortable hotel rooms through to spacious suites and family-friendly apartments, all designed with a relaxed beach-house feel. Guests have access to a resort-style pool club, lush garden areas, complimentary on-site parking and easy strolls to Toukley's beaches, lake foreshore, cafes and boutiques. Buffet breakfast is served daily, and the friendly team can help guide you to the very best of the Central Coast.
hotel.description_p3: Two on-site venues take care of dining: Pelicans Restaurant offers a refined, seafood-led menu in a light-filled lakeside setting, while Beachie Bar and Bistro turns out wood-fired pizzas, elevated pub classics and tropical cocktails with a casual, lively vibe. The resort also features multiple bars, the pool club, conference and event spaces, secure parking and beautifully landscaped grounds — everything you need for a weekend escape or a longer Central Coast stay.
hotel.description_headline: A waterfront icon at the heart of the Central Coast.

advertisers.name: MexiCoast Cantina
advertisers.hero_subtitle: Baja-inspired Mexican cooking, salt-rim margaritas and warm cantina colour on the northern Central Coast, a short coastal drive from Terrigal.
advertisers.description_p1: MexiCoast Cantina brings the sun-baked flavours of the Baja Peninsula to the Central Coast, with flame-grilled tacos, slow-cooked fillings and a tequila list that runs deep into mezcal territory. Everything is built around bright, generous plates designed to be shared across the table.
advertisers.description_p2: The room hums with cantina warmth: hand-painted touches, a busy bar shaking salt-rimmed margaritas, and a soundtrack that nudges you into holiday mode. It is the kind of dinner you settle into for a second round.
advertisers.description_headline: Baja flavours by the coast.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary margarita with any main meal.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page when ordering. Valid for guide-card holders, dine-in only, one per guest.

advertisers.name: Mangkorn Massage
advertisers.hero_subtitle: Traditional Thai massage and oil treatments in a calm Toukley studio, drawing on ancient pressure-point techniques to unwind tight shoulders and travel-tired legs.
advertisers.description_p1: Mangkorn, the Thai word for dragon, sets the tone here: power, grace and deep renewal. Trained therapists work through acupressure, rhythmic compression and assisted stretching to release tension and restore flow, with oil, hot stone, foot and cupping options on the menu.
advertisers.description_p2: The studio is quiet, warm and unhurried, with couples suites for paired bookings and short foot-focus sessions for the time-poor. It is an easy reset between beach days and dinner reservations.
advertisers.description_headline: Where pressure heals, stillness speaks.
advertisers.offer_headline: Ten percent off any 60 or 90 minute treatment.
advertisers.offer_body: Mention the hotel guide when booking and present this page on arrival. Bookings essential.

advertisers.name: Dunes by Dish
advertisers.address: Level 1, 101 Soldiers Point Drive, Norah Head NSW 2263
advertisers.hero_subtitle: An upstairs surf-club restaurant perched above Soldiers Beach, with sweeping ocean views, share-style seafood and tapas, and a cocktail list with a wink.
advertisers.description_p1: Tucked into the top floor of Soldiers Beach Surf Club, Dunes by Dish makes the most of one of the Coast's best uninterrupted ocean outlooks. The kitchen leans into local seafood, tapas plates and elevated pub classics, all designed for long lunches that drift into sunset.
advertisers.description_p2: Inside is breezy and casual, with timber, light and that ever-changing blue horizon doing most of the decorating. It suits a slow Sunday with friends as easily as a celebratory dinner with a view.
advertisers.description_headline: Above the dunes at Soldiers Beach.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary glass of house wine with any two mains.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page to your server when ordering. Dine-in only, one per guest, not valid with other offers.

advertisers.name: The Savoy Bar & Music
advertisers.address: 2/391 The Entrance Road, Long Jetty NSW 2261
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A 1950s cinema reborn as Long Jetty's late-night bar and music room, pouring natural wine and pulling Italian crowd-pleasers from the kitchen.
advertisers.description_p1: Behind the restored Savoy facade is a buzzy little venue that doubles as neighbourhood bar, music room and event space. The kitchen turns out Napoli-style pizzas, charcuterie and cheese boards, while the bar leans into natural wine, low-sulphur drops and creative cocktails.
advertisers.description_p2: Trivia on Wednesdays, open mic Thursdays and live music through the weekend keep the calendar humming. It is the sort of room you wander into for one drink and leave three hours later.
advertisers.description_headline: Live music in a restored cinema.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary Savoy spritz with any pizza ordered after 5pm.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the bar when ordering. One per guest, dine-in only.

advertisers.name: Plain Janes Store
advertisers.address: 346 The Entrance Road, Long Jetty NSW 2261
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A light-filled Long Jetty boutique stocking effortless women's wear, kids' pieces and homewares from local and Australian-made labels, curated by two sisters.
advertisers.description_p1: Plain Janes is the brainchild of fabric-loving sisters and Central Coast locals who have been shaping Long Jetty's main street since 2015. The racks are tightly edited: easy, wearable women's pieces, plus a thoughtful selection of kids' clothing, accessories and homewares.
advertisers.description_p2: The store is white-walled and bright, the kind of browse that feels like a treat rather than a chore. Pop in between brunch and the beach for a piece you will actually wear back home.
advertisers.description_headline: Simple, stylish, every day.
advertisers.offer_headline: Ten percent off any full-priced item in store.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the counter before payment. One transaction per guest, in store only.

advertisers.name: Cue & Crew
advertisers.address: Omega Centre, 2e Reliance Drive, Block E, Tuggerah NSW 2259
advertisers.hero_subtitle: Family-owned American smokehouse turning out low-and-slow ribs, brisket and pulled pork over iron-bark wood, with live music rolling through the weekend.
advertisers.description_p1: Cue & Crew has been smoking meat low and slow on the Central Coast since 2017, building a signature flavour over slow-burning iron bark. Expect tender brisket, fall-apart ribs and proper pulled pork, plus the all-you-can-eat midweek nights that have built a loyal local following.
advertisers.description_p2: The room is loud, friendly and family-friendly, with weekend live music from local artists keeping the energy up. It is built for groups, big appetites and one more round of sides.
advertisers.description_headline: Low and slow, Coast style.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary side of mac and cheese with any main.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page when ordering. Dine-in only, one per guest.

advertisers.name: Bateau Tuggerah
advertisers.hero_subtitle: Self-drive boat hire on the calm, shallow waters of Tuggerah Lake, with skipper-free vessels, fishing gear on tap and no licence required.
advertisers.description_p1: Bateau Tuggerah is built around the easy pleasure of an afternoon on the water. The fleet is set up for first-timers and families: stable, simple to handle and ready to go with bait, tackle and safety gear sorted at the dock.
advertisers.description_p2: Pack a picnic, point the bow toward a quiet shoreline and let the day unwind. The lake is calm, the wildlife is generous and you do not need a licence to take the wheel.
advertisers.description_headline: On the lake, no licence required.
advertisers.offer_headline: Ten percent off any half-day hire.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page when collecting your boat. Bookings recommended, subject to availability.

advertisers.name: Wildfire Day Spa
advertisers.address: Mercure Kooindah Waters, 38 Kooindah Boulevard, Wyong NSW 2259
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A luxurious destination spa inside Kooindah Waters Resort, with magnesium float pool, infrared sauna and couples suites set among golf-green fairways.
advertisers.description_p1: Wildfire Day Spa is tucked inside the Mercure Kooindah Waters Resort, with treatment rooms designed to feel a long way from the everyday. Therapists work with Bioline luxury skincare across massages, facials, body scrubs, soaks and full beauty services.
advertisers.description_p2: Two immersive couples suites, a magnesium float pool and an infrared sauna make it the kind of half-day you build the rest of the holiday around. It is unhurried, considered and quietly indulgent.
advertisers.description_headline: A proper Central Coast reset.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary float pool session with any 60-minute treatment.
advertisers.offer_body: Mention the hotel guide when booking and show this page on arrival. Subject to availability, bookings essential.

advertisers.name: Wyong Milk Factory
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A historic 1920s dairy factory reborn as a riverside precinct of cafe, tavern, cheese makers, chocolate makers and a playground for the kids.
advertisers.description_p1: Built by local dairy farmers in the 1920s, the Wyong Milk Factory is now a riverside precinct stitched together from a relaxed cafe, a family tavern, artisan cheese and chocolate makers and a generous playground. It is the rare venue that can absorb a whole afternoon without effort.
advertisers.description_p2: The Tavern handles pub classics, burgers, pizzas and a Thai menu alongside local beers and live music. The Cafe leans breakfast and lunch with kid-friendly options and plenty of room to spread out by the river.
advertisers.description_headline: A century-old factory, still feeding the Coast.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary kids meal with any adult main at the Tavern.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page when ordering at the Tavern. One per table, dine-in only.

advertisers.name: Central Coast Aero Club
advertisers.hero_subtitle: Scenic joy flights and pilot training from Warnervale Airport, with low-wing trips over the lakes, Sydney Harbour and the Hunter Valley vineyards.
advertisers.description_p1: Operating out of Warnervale Airport since the early 1970s, the Central Coast Aero Club is the Coast's home of light aviation. Scenic joy flights take in the Tuggerah Lakes, Sydney Harbour and the Hunter Valley, while the school trains everyone from first-timers up to commercial pilots.
advertisers.description_p2: Trial Instructional Flights put you at the controls within minutes of arrival, and the uncontrolled airfield means very little time spent waiting. It is the holiday memory that puts the rest of the trip into perspective.
advertisers.description_headline: See the Coast from the air.
advertisers.offer_headline: Ten percent off any scenic flight for guide-card holders.
advertisers.offer_body: Mention the hotel guide when booking and present this page on arrival. Subject to weather and availability.

advertisers.name: Amazement Farm & Fun Park
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A sprawling Central Coast farm and fun park where hedge mazes, friendly animals and Aussie wildlife share one unforgettable day out in Wyong Creek.
advertisers.description_p1: Tucked into the green hills of the Yarramalong Valley, Amazement Farm & Fun Park brings together three hand-grown hedge mazes, native wildlife encounters and a working farmyard on one wonderfully eccentric property. It is the rare attraction that delivers genuine surprises for both restless kids and quietly curious adults.
advertisers.description_p2: Expect bottle-feeding lambs, eye-to-eye moments with kangaroos and wombats, pedal carts, jumping pillows and that signature maze-solving sense of achievement. Pack a picnic, wear closed shoes and plan to lose a happy half-day to it.
advertisers.description_headline: Mazes, mobs and mischief in the Yarramalong Valley.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary animal-feed cup with every paid entry.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the front gate when you arrive to redeem.

advertisers.name: Iris Lodge Alpacas
advertisers.hero_subtitle: An award-winning, eco-certified alpaca farm in Jilliby where 145 gentle alpacas welcome small groups for hand-feeding, brunches and unhurried country mornings.
advertisers.description_p1: Iris Lodge is the kind of place you leave grinning involuntarily. Run by genuine alpaca obsessives, the farm has built its reputation on small groups, ethical animal care and an accessible, all-ages welcome that suits prams and wheelchairs as easily as it suits curious adults.
advertisers.description_p2: Choose a meet-and-greet for an hour with the herd, or stay longer for Brunch with Alpacas served paddock-side. It is calm, photogenic, slightly surreal and worth the gentle drive inland.
advertisers.description_headline: One hundred and forty-five alpacas. One very good morning.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary bag of alpaca feed with each booked experience.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at check-in when you arrive at the farm gate.

advertisers.name: Treetops Adventure
advertisers.address: Ourimbah State Forest, 1 Red Hill Road, Wyong Creek NSW 2259
advertisers.hero_subtitle: NSW's biggest high-ropes park, strung through the towering eucalypts of Ourimbah State Forest, with flying foxes, bridges and challenges for every nerve level.
advertisers.description_p1: Treetops Adventure turns a patch of Central Coast forest into a vertical playground of zip lines, swinging logs and rope bridges that rise through the canopy. With courses graded from cruisy family loops to genuinely heart-thumping black runs, it scales beautifully to whoever turns up.
advertisers.description_p2: Strap into a continuous-belay harness, listen carefully to the safety briefing, then disappear into the trees for two hours of self-paced climbing. Great for groups, sneaky for first dates and surprisingly meditative once you find your rhythm.
advertisers.description_headline: Into the canopy, on your own steam.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary commemorative photo download with each adult climb.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the welcome hut when you sign in for your session.

advertisers.name: Ken Duncan Gallery
advertisers.address: 414 The Entrance Road, Erina Heights NSW 2260
advertisers.hero_subtitle: One of Australia's largest privately owned photographic galleries, showcasing Ken Duncan's sweeping panoramic landscapes a few minutes from Terrigal in Erina Heights.
advertisers.description_p1: Ken Duncan's purpose-built gallery is a quietly remarkable space, with high ceilings, generous lighting and walls hung with the panoramic landscapes that have come to define how Australia sees itself. The scale of the prints rewards an unhurried visit.
advertisers.description_p2: Take your time through the viewing rooms and the theatre, then settle into the on-site cafe to look back over your favourites. It suits art lovers, road-trippers and anyone who enjoys big country seen through a thoughtful lens.
advertisers.description_headline: The wide brown land, beautifully framed.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary coffee at the gallery cafe with any gallery purchase.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the gallery counter when paying.

advertisers.name: Distillery Botanica
advertisers.hero_subtitle: An award-winning Central Coast gin distillery set among three acres of botanical gardens in Erina, with tastings, masterclasses and a relaxed cellar-door bar.
advertisers.description_p1: Distillery Botanica is the kind of place that quietly raises the bar for a region. Founder Philip Moore grows many of the botanicals on site, and the resulting gins and liqueurs are pleasingly idiosyncratic, with a signature Murraya bloom note running through the range.
advertisers.description_p2: Settle into the cellar door for a guided tasting flight, wander the gardens between sips, or book in for a distil-your-own gin masterclass. It is grown-up, unfussy and genuinely lovely on a slow afternoon.
advertisers.description_headline: A garden, a still, and a very good gin.
advertisers.offer_headline: Complimentary upgrade to the premium tasting flight with each ticketed tasting.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page to your host when seated at the tasting bar.

advertisers.name: Chocolate Factory Gosford
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A working chocolate and nougat factory in West Gosford where Bon Bon, Nougat Limar and Sydney Marshmallow Co share one deliciously fragrant roof.
advertisers.description_p1: This is the sweetest detour on the Central Coast and probably the most fragrant. Three artisan makers share the West Gosford site, so you can watch glossy chocolates being enrobed, slabs of nougat sliced and pillowy marshmallow set, all on the same visit.
advertisers.description_p2: Build your own chocolate bar at the counter, graze a tasting tray with the kids or stock up on gifts you have no intention of sharing. Perfect for a rainy morning or the back end of a beach day.
advertisers.description_headline: Behind the glass, the good stuff is being made.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary build-your-own chocolate bar with any in-store purchase over twenty dollars.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the counter when you place your order.

advertisers.name: Australian Reptile Park
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A much-loved Somersby wildlife park where venomous snake milking, croc shows and koala cuddles fund Australia's only antivenom programme of its kind.
advertisers.description_p1: The Reptile Park has been a Central Coast institution for decades, and it still hits the sweet spot between proper zoo and proper adventure. The keeper-led shows are genuinely lively, and the spider and snake venom programmes here save Australian lives every year.
advertisers.description_p2: Plan your day around the show schedule, meet Hugo the croc, get nose-to-nose with a Galapagos tortoise and finish at the dingoes. Strollers and wheelchairs roll easily; bring a hat and a sense of humour.
advertisers.description_headline: Scales, fangs and the country's bravest keepers.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary souvenir guidebook with every adult ticket purchased on arrival.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the ticket window on arrival.

advertisers.name: Coastal Hatters
advertisers.address: 189 Ocean View Road, Ettalong Beach NSW 2257
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A proper master hatter in the Ettalong Galleria, with more than three thousand sun-safe and styled hats and three decades of fitting know-how behind the counter.
advertisers.description_p1: Coastal Hatters is owned by Eric, a master hatter best known for many years at Sydney's Strand Hatters, and it shows. The store carries more than three thousand hats, with a strong lean toward Australian-made names like Akubra, Cancer Council and Canopy Bay.
advertisers.description_p2: Walk in for a free expert fitting, ask for a reshape on a hat you already own, or leave with a panama that finally suits your face. It is the antidote to the petrol-station bucket hat.
advertisers.description_headline: The right hat, fitted properly, for the rest of your life.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary hat elastic and professional fitting with any hat purchased in store.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page in store before your fitting.

advertisers.name: Broken Bay Pearl Farm
advertisers.hero_subtitle: NSW's only pearl farm, hidden on the lower Hawkesbury River, where guided cruises reveal how Australian Akoya pearls are grown, harvested and graded.
advertisers.description_p1: There is something quietly extraordinary about stepping onto a working pearl lease an hour north of Sydney and learning that Akoya pearls really are being grown right here. The two-hour tour combines a scenic Hawkesbury cruise with a hands-on look at oyster opening and pearl grading.
advertisers.description_p2: It suits curious travellers, jewellery lovers and anyone who enjoys a story well told on the water. Bring a jacket for the river breeze, leave time to browse the gem-grade harvest at the end.
advertisers.description_headline: Saltwater, sunlight and the patient making of pearls.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary keepsake Akoya pearl with each booked farm tour for two.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at the Kowan Road check-in shed before boarding.

advertisers.name: Pelicans Restaurant
advertisers.hero_subtitle: A breezy, seafood-led dining room at The Beachcomber where coastal flavours meet a relaxed, light-filled Hamptons setting beside Tuggerah Lake.
advertisers.description_p1: Pelicans Restaurant is the signature dining room at The Beachcomber Hotel & Resort, set in an airy, light-filled space with timber floors, cane pendants and soft mint-green banquettes. The menu leans into the lake and ocean on its doorstep, with a seafood-inspired offering balanced by modern Australian favourites built around quality local produce.
advertisers.description_p2: Open for daily buffet breakfast and an elegant evening service, Pelicans is equally at home for a long, leisurely meal with a glass of crisp white or a quiet dinner before retiring upstairs. Service is warm and unhurried, the wine list is thoughtfully chosen, and the atmosphere walks the line beautifully between special-occasion and easy-going coastal dining.
advertisers.description_headline: Coastal-modern dining at The Beachie.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary glass of house wine with any main.
advertisers.offer_body: Mention the Beachcomber Guide when you book and enjoy a complimentary glass of house red, white or sparkling with any main. One drink per diner, dine-in only.

advertisers.name: Beachie Bar and Bistro
advertisers.hero_subtitle: The Beachcomber's casual all-day bar and bistro, turning out wood-fired pizzas, elevated pub classics and tropical cocktails on the lakeside veranda.
advertisers.description_p1: Beachie Bar and Bistro is the fun, easy-going heart of The Beachcomber — a lakeside bar and bistro built for long lunches, sunset drinks and shared plates with friends. Pull up to the veranda overlooking the water and settle in with a tropical cocktail, a cold local beer or something from a tightly curated wine list.
advertisers.description_p2: The kitchen turns out crowd-pleasing pub classics done well alongside crispy wood-fired pizzas, fresh salads and generous share plates. With its breezy coastal fit-out, regular live entertainment and family-friendly atmosphere, Beachie Bar and Bistro captures everything locals love about The Beachie — and is the perfect first stop after check-in.
advertisers.description_headline: Easy lakeside drinking and dining at The Beachie.
advertisers.offer_headline: A complimentary wood-fired pizza with any two mains.
advertisers.offer_body: Show this page at Beachie Bar and Bistro and receive a complimentary classic Margherita pizza when you order any two mains. Dine-in only, one per table, not valid with other promotions.
